    FederalOpen

    Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance for Clean Energy Equipment (Classes 43.1 and 43.2)

    Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)

    Tax credit

    Accelerated depreciation: 30% CCA rate (Class 43.1); 50% (Class 43.2, property acquired before 2025); enhanced first-year allowance proposed for Class 43.1 property acquired 2025-2033

    Lets businesses write off qualifying clean energy generation and energy conservation equipment (e.g., solar, wind, heat recovery, certain storage) faster than ordinary equipment, lowering taxable income in early years.

    Eligibility and details
    Eligibility
    Businesses earning business income in Canada (corporations, sole proprietors, partnerships) that acquire property meeting the Class 43.1/43.2 definitions. Some fossil-fuelled and low-efficiency waste-fuelled equipment is restricted for property available after 2024.
    Deadline
    Ongoing
    Industries
    All industries
    Who can apply
    Small & medium business, Large business, Startup
    Purpose
    Clean technology & energy efficiency, Equipment & capital investment

    Last checked: 2026-11-11

    FederalOpen

    Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance for Zero-Emission Vehicles and Equipment (Classes 54, 55 and 56)

    Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)

    Tax credit

    Accelerated write-off (tax deduction, not a credit): regular declining-balance CCA rates of 30% (Class 54; passenger vehicles capped at $61,000 plus taxes), 40% (Class 55) and 30% (Class 56), plus an enhanced first-year allowance (currently 55% for property acquired in 2026-2027; proposed 100% for property acquired after 2024 and available for use before 2030, then 75% and 55% to 2033)

    Lets businesses deduct the cost of fully electric or hydrogen vehicles and zero-emission equipment (e.g., trucks, buses, boats, locomotives) much faster than ordinary vehicles.

    Eligibility and details
    Eligibility
    Businesses that acquire eligible zero-emission vehicles (Classes 54/55, as defined by CRA) or fully electric or hydrogen-powered automotive equipment and vehicles other than motor vehicles (Class 56) for business use. An election can be made not to include a vehicle in these classes.
    Deadline
    Ongoing (proposed enhanced rates for property available before 2034)
    Industries
    All industries
    Who can apply
    Small & medium business, Large business, Startup
    Purpose
    Clean technology & energy efficiency, Equipment & capital investment

    Last checked: 2026-11-11

    How to use this list

    Before you apply.

    A few rules apply to most government funding programs in Canada.

    Check eligibility on the official page

    Each card links to the program's official page. Read the eligibility rules, eligible costs and the application guide there before you plan around a program.

    Apply before you spend

    Most grants and contributions only cover costs incurred after your application is approved. Spending first can make a cost ineligible.

    Know the stacking limits

    Many programs cap the total government funding on one project, often at 50% to 75% of eligible costs. Disclose all other public funding you receive.

    Keep good records

    Approved projects usually need receipts, timesheets and progress reports before claims are paid. Set up tracking from day one.

    Disclaimer

    This directory is for general information only. Programs, amounts and deadlines change often. Always confirm details on the official program page before you apply. Chmltech is not affiliated with any government program and does not decide funding applications.
